content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge counts Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 toward breaking C3 but neither quotes an earlier-round sentence pressing those verses against the link nor names that round.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"The phrase 'counts as an unanswered witness only when' — I weighed (1) it applies to any verse the judge counts toward a broken link, including verses recited in the judge's own reasoning; (2) it applies only to verses appearing on a side's 'cited in' line, not to independently cited verses.","why":"The judge counts Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 toward a broken link without quoting an earlier-round sentence pressing them against that link or a listed premise and without naming the round, so it breaches K-G4."}
